title: So-Called Dollars
citation: Harold E. Hibler and Charles V. Kappen. 1st ed., Coin and Currency Institute, 1963; 2nd ed. 2008, revised by Tom Hoffman, Dave Hayes, Jonathan Brecher and John Dean.
covers: American commemorative, exposition and monetary medals of roughly 33 to 45 mm, from 1826 into the 1960s. The second edition added numbers above 1000 for pieces the first missed, and letter suffixes for varieties.
lookup_label: So-Called Dollars online, by HK number
find_note: Second edition, in print.

aliases: Standard Catalog of United States Tokens
title: Standard Catalog of United States Tokens 1700–1900
citation: Russell Rulau. Krause Publications: 1st ed. 1994, 2nd 1997, 3rd 1999, 4th 2004. Consolidates his earlier Early American Tokens, Hard Times Tokens, U.S. Merchant Tokens 1845–1860, U.S. Trade Tokens 1866–1889 and Tokens of the Gay Nineties.
covers: American tokens of every kind from 1700 to 1900, arranged by period and then by state and city. The prefix tells you the period: E for early American, HT for Hard Times, state-city codes for the merchant and trade-token sections.
example: Rulau E-Pa 1, Rulau Pa-Ph 12, Rulau IL-EL-6
notes: Washington pieces inside Rulau are cited by Baker number instead. On a Swiss shooting medal, R- means Richter.
find_label: Out of print; search the Newman Portal
find_note: All editions out of print; the fourth is the one to look for secondhand.

title: Hard Times Tokens 1832–1844
citation: Russell Rulau. Krause Publications, editions 1980 to 1996; then The Standard Catalog of Hard Times Tokens, 2001. A revision and enlargement of Lyman Low's 1899 list, and the same numbers appear inside the Standard Catalog of U.S. Tokens.
covers: The political, satirical and merchant tokens of the Jackson and Van Buren years, 1832 to 1844, renumbered and expanded well beyond Low. The book carries a concordance to Low numbers.
find_label: Out of print; search the Newman Portal
find_note: Out of print.

title: Hard Times Tokens
citation: Lyman Haynes Low. New York, published by the author, 1899; 2nd ed., revised and enlarged, 1900; supplement 1906. Reprinted 1955 and by Durst in 1978 and 1984.
covers: The original 183-number list of Hard Times tokens. Low numbers are still quoted beside the Rulau HT numbers that replaced them.
lookup_label: 1900 edition scanned on the Internet Archive
find_note: 1900 edition.

title: U.S. Civil War Store Cards, and Patriotic Civil War Tokens
citation: George and Melvin Fuld. Store Cards: 1st ed. Quarterman 1972, 3rd ed. Civil War Token Society 2014 (rev. John Ostendorf), 4th ed. 2024. Patriotics: 1st ed. Whitman 1960, 6th ed. Civil War Token Society 2018.
covers: Civil War tokens of 1861 to 1865. Store cards are numbered by state, town, merchant and die pair; patriotics by obverse die, reverse die and a metal letter (a is copper).
example: F-OH165A-1a (a Cincinnati store card), F-1/391a (a patriotic)
lookup_label: Civil War Token Society addenda to the current editions
find_note: Current editions, sold only by the society; members pay less.

title: The Provincial Token-Coinage of the 18th Century
citation: Richard Dalton and Samuel H. Hamer. Issued in fourteen parts, 1910 to 1918; reprinted 1967, 1977, 1990 and 2004.
covers: The British and Irish provincial copper tokens of 1787 to 1804, the Conder tokens, arranged by county with a running number inside each county and letters for die varieties.
find_note: Reprints out of print; the club's library page lists the free historical Conder books.

title: The Atwood-Coffee Catalogue of United States and Canadian Transportation Tokens
citation: American Vecturist Association. Roland Atwood's original 1958; 4th ed. 1983 by John M. Coffee Jr. and Harold V. Ford; 6th ed. 2007; 7th ed. 2016; 8th ed. 2023, edited by Joel Bernstein.
covers: Transit, ferry, bridge and toll tokens of the United States and Canada. The number is a state abbreviation, a city number and a letter for each issue; Canadian entries use the province. Pueblo is CO 760.
example: AC NY 630 A, Atwood CO 760 G
lookup_label: AVA catalog page; the PDF is free to members
find_note: Eighth edition; the PDF is free to members.

title: A Century of Campaign Buttons 1789–1889
citation: J. Doyle DeWitt. Hartford, privately published, 1959.
covers: Political campaign medalets, tokens, ferrotypes and lapel pieces, numbered by candidate initials, year and a serial.
notes: Sullivan's 1981 revision keeps the same scheme and extends it to 1892; dealers write Sullivan/DeWitt.
find_note: Out of print.

title: American Political Badges and Medalets 1789–1892
citation: Edmund B. Sullivan. Quarterman Publications, 1981.
covers: DeWitt's list revised and extended through 1892, same candidate-year-number format, with new numbers added for pieces DeWitt did not know.
find_label: Out of print; search the Newman Portal
find_note: Out of print.

title: Medallic Portraits of Washington
citation: William Spohn Baker, Philadelphia, 1885. Revised by Russell Rulau and George Fuld as Medallic Portraits of Washington, Krause 1985; 2nd ed. 1999.
covers: Every medal, token, store card and coin bearing George Washington. Baker's 651 numbers were kept by Rulau and Fuld, who added letters for varieties and new numbers above his.
lookup_label: 1885 edition scanned on the Internet Archive
find_note: 1885 edition; the Rulau-Fuld revision is out of print.

aliases: Medals of the United States Mint
title: Medals of the United States Mint: The First Century 1792–1892
citation: R. W. Julian, edited by N. Neil Harris. Token and Medal Society, 1977.
covers: Medals struck by the Mint in its first hundred years, in classes with two-letter codes: IP Indian peace, PR presidential, MI military, NA naval, CM commemorative, LS life saving, AC Assay Commission, PE personal, and others.
example: Julian IP-3, Julian PR-12, Julian CM-20
find_note: Out of print.

title: American Colonial History Illustrated by Contemporary Medals
citation: C. Wyllys Betts, edited by Frederic H. Betts, William T. R. Marvin and Lyman H. Low. Scott Stamp and Coin Co., 1894. Reprinted 1970 and 1972; companion volume by Christopher McDowell, ANS 2022.
covers: European and American medals relating to the Americas from about 1556 to 1783, in nine chronological periods: 623 numbers.
lookup_label: 1894 edition scanned on the Internet Archive
find_note: The 1894 book is a free scan; McDowell's Early Betts Medal Companion (2022) is sold by the ANS.

aliases: Medallic History of the United States
title: The Medallic History of the United States of America 1776–1876
citation: J. F. Loubat, with etched plates by Jules Jacquemart. New York, published by the author, 1878; reprinted 1967.
covers: The eighty-six medals voted by Congress and the other national medals of the first century, numbered 1 to 86.
lookup_label: Volume one scanned on the Internet Archive; also on Project Gutenberg
find_note: Also scanned on the Internet Archive.

title: British Commemorative Medals and their Values
citation: Christopher Eimer. Seaby, 1987; 2nd ed. Spink, 2010, about 2,200 medals.
covers: British commemorative and historical medals from the sixteenth century to the present, in one running sequence.
find_note: Second edition, in print.

title: A Catalogue of British Historical Medals 1760–1960
citation: Laurence Brown. Vol. I, George III to William IV, Seaby 1980; Vol. II, Victoria, 1987; Vol. III, Edward VII to 1960, Spink 1995.
covers: British historical medals from 1760 to 1960, one running number across the three volumes.
find_note: Volumes come and go; otherwise secondhand.

title: Edkins' Catalogue of United States Coal Company Store Scrip
citation: Donald O. Edkins for the National Scrip Collectors Association. 1st ed. 1977; 4th ed. Vol. I (all states but West Virginia) 2015, with Garrett Salyers and Mike Williams; Vol. II, West Virginia.
covers: Coal and lumber company scrip tokens by state, county and company, with a serial for each company and a letter-number for each piece, plus rarity ratings. Colorado material would be in Volume I.
lookup_label: NSCA revisions and updates to the listings
find_note: The association publishes and sells it.

title: Civil War Sutler Tokens and Cardboard Scrip
citation: David E. Schenkman. Jade House, 1983; 2nd ed. 2014, edited by Richard W. Irons.
covers: Tokens and cardboard scrip issued by the sutlers who followed Union and Confederate regiments, numbered by state, regiment, denomination and metal; the unattributed series is prefixed US.
find_label: Out of print; search the Newman Portal
find_note: Second edition 2014; ask the Civil War Token Society or a numismatic bookseller.

title: Lincoln in Numismatics
citation: Robert P. King, serialized in The Numismatist from February 1924 with supplements to 1933; reprinted by the Token and Medal Society 1966 and by Durst 1985. Superseded by Paul Cunningham's Lincoln's Metallic Imagery, which carries a concordance.
covers: Medals, tokens and related pieces portraying Abraham Lincoln.
lookup_label: The original Numismatist issues, full view on the Newman Portal
find_label: Free, The Numismatist on the Newman Portal
find_note: The 1924–1933 serial; the reprints are out of print.

title: California Tokens
citation: Charles V. Kappen. Token and Medal Society, 1976; supplement 1998.
covers: California merchant and trade tokens, by town.
find_label: Out of print; search the Newman Portal
find_note: Out of print.

title: A Guide to Colorado Merchant Trade Tokens
citation: Stuart M. Pritchard Jr. Jinglebob Press, Louisville, Colorado, 2004.
covers: Colorado trade tokens by town. Numbers are a two-letter town code and a serial: PU Pueblo, DE Denver, TR Trinidad, LA Lamar and so on. The current standard; see our Pueblo page.
find_note: Out of print; copies turn up from Colorado dealers and online.

title: Colorado Merchants' Tokens
citation: James R. Wright with Herbert Lee Nott (earlier with Don Cary). Self-published 1973, with supplements in 1977 and 1979 continuing the numbers.
covers: The earlier Colorado trade-token catalog. CMT numbers survive in auction descriptions from the 1980s and 1990s; Pritchard replaced them in 2004.
find_note: Out of print; secondhand only.

title: TokenCatalog.com record number
citation: Richard Greever's online database, continuously updated by contributors.
covers: Not a book: a TC number is the record number of a token in the TokenCatalog database, which holds more than 700,000 listings with issuer attributions where contributors have found them.
lookup_label: TokenCatalog; search by state and town, or by TC number
find_note: Free to browse.

title: Zerbe numbers for Lesher Referendum dollars
citation: Farran Zerbe, "Private Silver Coins Issued in the United States: The Lesher or Referendum Pieces," American Journal of Numismatics 51, 1917.
covers: The eighteen varieties of Joseph Lesher's 1900 and 1901 Colorado silver dollars, numbered Z-1 to Z-18. They run parallel to HK-787 to 797 and HK-1016 to 1021a.
lookup_label: Our Lesher page, with the full HK and Zerbe concordance
find_note: AJN volumes 51–53. Leonard, Hallenbeck and Wilde's 2017 book is in print from Arcadia Publishing.

title: Society of Medalists issue number
citation: The subscription series of American art medals, 1930 to 1995, issue by issue.
covers: Each Society of Medalists issue, from SOM-1 (Laura Gardin Fraser's Hunter and Grouse, 1930) to the last in 1995, with the special issues and variants.
lookup_label: Every issue listed at Medallic Art Collector
find_note: The series itself is collected, not bought as a book.

aliases: One Hundred Years of American Medallic Art
title: One Hundred Years of American Medallic Art, 1845–1945: The John E. Marqusee Collection
citation: Susan Luftschein. Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art, Cornell University, 1995.
covers: The four hundred and more American art medals in the Marqusee collection, now at Cornell, in catalog order.
lookup_label: Listed by Marqusee number at Medallic Art Collector
find_note: Out of print; the listings are online at Medallic Art Collector.

aliases: Medals of the United States Mint Issued for Public Sale
title: Medals of the United States Mint Issued for Public Sale
citation: Kenneth M. Failor and Eleonora Hayden. U.S. Treasury, 1969; revised 1972; later Mint reprints.
covers: The medals the Mint sells to the public, presidential, secretarial, military and commemorative, under the three-digit Mint list numbers that the Mint's own catalogs still use.
find_note: Out of print.

title: Numismatics of Massachusetts
citation: Malcolm Storer. Massachusetts Historical Society, 1923; reprinted by Quarterman, 1981.
covers: Massachusetts medals, tokens and related pieces in one running sequence; the Pilgrim Tercentenary medals, for instance, are Storer 1558 to 1563.
lookup_label: 1981 reprint scanned on the Internet Archive
find_note: 1981 reprint.

title: The American Store or Business Cards
citation: Dr. Benjamin P. Wright, serialized in The Numismatist 1898 to 1901; collected by the Token and Medal Society 1963 and reissued as American Business Tokens, Quarterman 1972.
covers: Nineteenth-century American merchant store cards, with rarity ratings.
notes: Not the same Wright as the Colorado catalog; those are CMT numbers.
lookup_label: The 1898–1901 Numismatist issues on the Newman Portal
find_note: The 1898–1901 serial is free on the Newman Portal.

title: Comitia Americana and Related Medals
citation: John W. Adams and Anne E. Bentley. George Frederick Kolbe, 2007.
covers: The Congressional medals of the Revolution, the Libertas Americana and the diplomatic medals, with die and variety analysis. Cited alongside Betts numbers.
find_note: Out of print; ask Kolbe & Fanning or a numismatic bookseller.

title: Vlack numbers
citation: Robert A. Vlack. Early American Coins (1965; 2nd ed. 1974) for the imitation British halfpence; An Illustrated Catalogue of the French Billon Coinage in the Americas, Colonial Coin Collectors Club, 2004.
covers: Two series. The imitation George III halfpence of 1771 to 1788, numbered by obverse and by a reverse code of date and letter; and the French colonial billon for the Americas.
find_note: The French billon catalog, with the club's dealer link. Early American Coins is out of print.

aliases: Guide Book of United States Tokens and Medals
title: A Guide Book of United States Tokens and Medals; 100 Greatest American Medals and Tokens
citation: Katherine Jaeger, Whitman 2008; Katherine Jaeger and Q. David Bowers, Whitman 2007.
covers: Illustrated overviews rather than numbering systems; both cite HK, Baker, Julian and the rest. The 100 Greatest ranks its pieces 1 to 100, and dealers occasionally quote the rank.
find_note: In print.

title: Merchant and Privately Countermarked Coins: Advertising on the World’s Smallest Billboards
citation: Gregory G. Brunk. World Exonumia Press, Rockford, Illinois, 2003; 476 pages. The second edition of his catalogue, combining American and Canadian Countermarked Coins (1987) and Merchant Countermarks on World Coins (1989).
covers: Coins stamped with a merchant’s or a private person’s name or mark, worldwide. Each number is a letter and a number, the letter taken from the name in the stamp.
notes: Rulau’s Standard Catalog numbers American counterstamps too, so lot descriptions often give both, as in Brunk H-701, Rulau Z46g. The 1987 book numbered differently, as in Brunk-40L (1880).
lookup_label: The 1987 American and Canadian edition, free on the Internet Archive
find_note: The 2003 book is out of print; look secondhand. The Internet Archive item dated 2006 under the same title is Brunk’s draft revision, not the book.

title: The Medals of Karl Goetz
citation: Gunter W. Kienast. The Artus Company, Cleveland, 1967; 284 pages, 500 numbered copies. Supplement: Goetz II, The Artus Company, Lincoln, Nebraska, 1986; 179 pages.
covers: The medals of the German medallist Karl Goetz, in one running number. Goetz made 633 medals, about 175 of them satirical, the First World War pieces best known among them.
notes: NGC labels write KIENAST-246; NGC’s census spells the category “Keinast”.
find_note: Both volumes are out of print in their original editions; a softcover reprint of the pair was announced in 2013.

title: Philippine Medals and Tokens
citation: Earl D. Honeycutt. 1st ed. (1780–2010), Mactanboy Press, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, 2014; 2nd ed. (1780–2015), 2017; 3rd ed. (1780–2020), 2020; 4th ed. (1780–2024), with Sandy Lichauco, 2024.
covers: Medals and tokens of the Philippines from 1780 to the present. The third edition listed 1,882 pieces.
notes: Reviews cross-reference the older Basso numbers, as in Honeycutt 322 = Basso 166.
find_label: The E-Sylum’s notice of the fourth edition
find_note: In 2024 the authors offered it directly; the notice has the details.

title: Die Schützentaler und Schützenmedaillen der Schweiz (Swiss Shooting Thalers and Shooting Medals)
citation: Jürg Richter. 1st ed. 2005; 2nd ed. Battenberg Gietl Verlag, Regenstauf, 2018; 564 pages, German with full English text.
covers: Swiss shooting-festival thalers and medals from the early seventeenth century to 1960, more than 2,500 pieces, each with a rarity rating and valuations.
notes: NGC labels write R-1958a: on a Swiss shooting piece, R means Richter, not Rulau. Older citations use Martin numbers (Jean L. Martin, Swiss Shooting Medals 1612–1939, Galerie des Monnaies, Lausanne, 1972), as in Martin 330, or Delbert Ray Krause’s Swiss Shooting Talers and Medals (Whitman, 1965).
lookup_label: The publisher’s free sample: introduction and how to read an entry
find_note: Second edition, in print.

title: Bimetallic Trade Tokens of the United States
citation: David E. Schenkman. Jade House Publications, 1990.
covers: American trade tokens made of two metals, from George G. Greenburg’s patent through the type’s life of less than forty years. Listed alphabetically by issuer, with an index by state.
notes: That is how NGC labels them. Schenkman also wrote the sutler-token catalogue; the token itself tells you which book is meant.
lookup_label: TokenCatalog, which cites this book
find_note: Look for it secondhand.

aliases: Military Tokens of the United States
title: Military Tokens of the United States
citation: Paul A. Cunningham. Vol. I, Domestic Issues, Michigan Exonumia Publishers, Tecumseh, Michigan, 1995, 440 pages; Vol. 2, Overseas Issues, 1998, 461 pages.
covers: Tokens issued at United States armed-forces installations, such as post exchanges and NCO messes. Volume I covers installations inside the United States, by state and then installation; volume 2 the overseas ones.
notes: The earlier listing is James J. Curto’s Military Tokens of the United States, 1866–1969 (Krause, 1970).
lookup_label: TokenCatalog, which cites Cunningham numbers
find_note: Look for it secondhand.

title: Thomas L. Elder, A Catalogue of His Tokens and Medals
citation: Thomas K. DeLorey. The Numismatist, June and July 1980.
covers: The tokens, store cards and medals issued by the New York coin dealer Thomas L. Elder, about 640 pieces.
notes: Lots often add another catalogue’s number, as in DeLorey-9, Eglit-64.
lookup_label: The June 1980 Numismatist, free on the Internet Archive
find_label: The July 1980 issue, where it concludes
find_note: Both issues are free scans.

title: Bryan Money
citation: Fred Schornstein. Token and Medal Society, 2001. A revision of Farran Zerbe’s catalogue, “Bryan Money: Tokens of the Presidential Campaigns of 1896 and 1900, Comparative and Satirical,” The Numismatist, July 1926.
covers: The comparative and satirical pieces of William Jennings Bryan’s 1896 and 1900 presidential campaigns, the free-silver mock dollars among them.
notes: That is how NGC labels them. NGC’s SCH-GM- labels on Benjamin Franklin medals are a different catalogue.
lookup_label: Zerbe’s 1926 original, free on the Internet Archive
find_note: No longer offered by the Token and Medal Society; look secondhand.

title: British Copper Tokens 1811–1820: Including Those of Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands
citation: Paul and Bente R. Withers. Galata Print, Llanfyllin, 1999; 264 pages.
covers: The copper tokens issued in Britain and Ireland from 1811 to 1820, the second token period after the Conder tokens of the 1790s.
notes: That is how NGC labels them; NGC files them as “Great Britain - Copper Tokens (1811-1820) listed in Withers”.
find_note: Look for it from numismatic booksellers.
